title: Fold a produce crate flat for return
instruction: Fold the empty crate flat for return, and finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Reusable folding plastic crates carry fresh produce from growers to stores. Once emptied at the store or distribution centre they are folded flat and stacked for the return truck, by hand: by packers and packagers (SOC 53-7064, about 0.6 million US workers, BLS) and by stockers and order fillers (53-7065, about 2.8 million), whose O*NET tasks include "Pack and unpack items to be stocked on shelves in stockrooms, warehouses, or storage yards." On crates whose end walls have a catch at each corner, both catches of an end wall must be pressed in together while the wall is tipped in; the end walls fold first and the long walls then fold down on top of them.
setup: Left and right are the robot's; positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top (the bare table, 75 cm high). One object: an empty green polypropylene folding produce crate (a returnable plastic container), 400 x 300 x 174 mm outside, 0.88 kg, standing up on the bench centred at (0.23, 0.00), its 400 mm length along x, so one short end wall faces the robot and the other faces away. Base: a 6 mm lattice floor, side rims 68 mm tall along the long sides, end rims 48 mm tall at the ends, all 10 mm thick. Walls: 10 mm plates hinged at the inner top edge of their rims, folding inward, with stops at upright and at flat. The two short end walls (270 x 126 mm) each have a 120 x 36 mm handhold under a 16 mm round top rail; the two long walls (396 x 106 mm) have a 14 mm round top rail and vents. Catches: each end wall is latched to the long walls by a sprung catch at each of its top corners. Each catch has a 16 x 16 mm thumb button on the outer face of the top rail, 100 mm either side of the wall's middle (200 mm apart), standing 6 mm proud; pressed in 3.5 mm or more it frees its corner (button spring 3 N at rest, 9 N flush). An end wall swings in only while both its buttons are held in; tipped in past its catches it folds down onto its rim. The long walls are held up by the end walls' catches: once neither end wall is latched, each can be pushed in over its stop and folds down on top of the end walls. Folded flat the crate is 80 mm tall: end walls lowest, long walls 5-10 mm above them. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Followed over the whole trial: 0 for good if the crate falls off the bench (its base more than 10 cm below the bench top) or if a catch is forced, that is a latched end wall, or a long wall held up by a latched end wall, pushed in more than 3 degrees (about 30 N at its top rail). Judged at the end, on live states, a wall lies flat when it is within 5 degrees of its folded stop. 1.0: all four walls flat with the long walls over the flat end walls, the folded crate under 90 mm tall at its highest point, its base on the bench and within 3 degrees of level, and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start). Otherwise 0.2 for each end wall lying flat plus 0.2 for each long wall lying flat over both flat end walls, at most 0.8. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the crate and its walls still. In a real trial: measure the folded height with a ruler (under 90 mm); check from the video that the end walls went down first and the long walls lie on top; check that no catch was forced (each end wall still clicks into both catches when stood back up); check the arms against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Lift each long wall up onto its stop, then swing each end wall up until both its catches click. Put the erect crate back centred at (0.23, 0.00), its length along x.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim (PhysX, 240 Hz) at real size and mass: base and four solid-plate walls (real walls are ribbed lattices) on hinges with stops, four 10 g buttons on sprung slides. Catches simplified: a stiff hinge spring holds a latched wall up and lets go while both its buttons are in 3.5 mm or more. Button size, travel and forces are estimates, not measured. PP friction 0.35.
